ai.description: This 2–3 cm frog is lime-green with a distinct white or yellow lateral stripe. It features large, adhesive toe pads and a translucent belly. It belongs to the family Rhacophoridae.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Rhacophorus lateralis* is uniquely distinguished by a distinct, thin white or yellow lateral stripe running along the sides of its body, which is absent in similar species.
ai.habitat: *Rhacophorus lateralis* inhabits evergreen and semi-evergreen forests in the Western Ghats, typically found on low-lying vegetation at altitudes between 800 and 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: *Rhacophorus lateralis* is primarily nocturnal, spending its nights foraging for small insects among the leaves of low-hanging vegetation.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Rhacophorus lateralis* breeds during the monsoon, laying small clutches of 10–20 eggs inside folded leaves suspended over water, which hatch into aquatic tadpoles.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Rhacophorus lateralis* is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, primarily occurring in the states of Karnataka, Kerala, and Tamil Nadu at elevations of 800–1,500m.
ai.callDescription: The Small Tree Frog emits a high-pitched, insect-like "tink" or "click" sound, typically heard from vegetation surrounding stagnant forest pools or marshes.
